review_method: Fresh visual inspection of retained official Katmai map pixels, independently rerendered from the original PDF, and both pages of the Naknek boating guide. Every selected source and rendered polygon part and ring was viewed in full. Ordered positions, bounds and ring closure were independently recomputed from the retained source collection and selected decoded baseline. Regional relative position, orientation, outline and neighbouring named waters were used together; bounds or label overlap alone were not used. Original packed decoding was not independently replayed. Independent observations were recorded before source-worker comparison.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; component water names do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: No additional work is needed for this bounded generalized identity. Exact shoreline, formal-registry or product-name application would require a separately authorized assessment.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete west-to-east generalized footprint has a broad rounded western basin and a narrower eastern continuation. Its position south of Kukaklek Lake, west of the separately mapped Kulik Lake, and east of the Nonvianuk River matches the water polygon directly labelled NONVIANUK LAKE on the official Katmai park map. The complete source and rendered ring support Nonvianuk Lake as a generalized water identity. This is a regional visual correspondence, not a surveyed shoreline or exact lake-to-river boundary.
limits: The coarse ring omits mapped shoreline detail and islands; no exact shoreline or inclusion of every inlet is certified.
Kulik Lake and the Nonvianuk River are separately mapped nearby waters; their names are not extended onto this lake or treated as aliases.
The NPS map is official cartographic usage, not a verified formal naming registry or current naming decision.

findings.follow_up_scope: Resolve the inter-lake and connecting-channel name boundary with more detailed direct evidence before separately authorized scalar naming or subdivision.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete generalized footprint begins with a northwestern north-south arm, bends southeast into a long eastward middle basin, and turns southeast again at its eastern end. The official Katmai park map labels the northwestern water LAKE COVILLE and the eastward/southeastern water LAKE GROSVENOR, with a narrow connection near Grosvenor Lodge. Both mapped waters correspond to portions of this single continuous inventory ring. No one-name identity for the complete polygon is established; Lake Coville and Lake Grosvenor are retained as separately labelled component waters. The precise inter-lake or connecting-channel name boundary is unresolved.
limits: One inventory Polygon does not imply one real-world lake name. Neither Lake Coville nor Lake Grosvenor is approved as a scalar name for the whole footprint.
The mapped narrow connection is generalized in the inventory; no exact split line, connecting-channel name, separate source geometry or repaired topology is supplied.
The boating guide is a Naknek-focused document and does not resolve the complete Coville-Grosvenor naming boundary.
Formal naming decisions, exact shorelines and Korean names are not established.

findings.supported_name_scope: The complete compact southwest-to-northeast generalized footprint matches the water directly labelled LAKE BROOKS on the official Katmai park map. Its northeastern end lies by Brooks River and Brooks Camp, southwest of the Naknek Lake and Iliuk Arm waters shown separately on the map. The full-lake page of the Naknek boating guide supplies additional regional shoreline and Brooks Camp context, without providing another certified selected-lake name in this review. The complete source and rendered ring support Lake Brooks as a generalized water identity, with exact shoreline, islands and lake-to-river boundary unverified.
limits: The single 15-position ring strongly generalizes shorelines and omits mapped islands; this is not surveyed feature coverage.
The direct supported word order is Lake Brooks; no additional alias or Korean form is certified.
Brooks River, Brooks Camp, Naknek Lake and Iliuk Arm provide location context and are not aliases for the selected lake.
The boating guide uses a separate regional presentation from the same NPS publisher; underlying cartographic independence is not established.
